---
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
a) A function $\phi :{\cal K}(V) \longrightarrow \mathbb{C}$ is called a valuation
if for any $K_1, \, K_2 \in {\cal K}(V)$ such that their union is
also convex one has
$$\phi(K_1 \cup K_2)= \phi(K_1) +\phi(K_2) -\phi(K_1 \cap K_2).$$

b) A valuation $\phi$ is called continuous if it is continuous
with respect to the Hausdorff metric on ${\cal K}(V)$.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- definition-2: body_md -->
A valuation $\phi$ is called polynomial of degree at most $d$ if
for every $K\in {\cal K}(V)$ the function $x\mapsto \phi (K+x)$ is
a polynomial on $V$ of degree at most $d$.
<!-- end definition-2 -->
<!-- example-1: body_md -->
(1) The Euler characteristic $\chi$ is a continuous translation
invariant valuation (remind that $\chi(K)=1$ for any convex
compact set $K$).

(2) Let $\mu$ be a measure on $V$ with a polynomial density with
respect to a Lebesgue measure. Fix $A\in {\cal K}(V)$. Then
$$\phi(K):=\mu (K+A)$$ is a continuous polynomial
valuation (here $K+A:=\{k+a|k\in K,\, a\in A\}$).
<!-- end example-1 -->
<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
In \cite{alesker-icm} we have announced a result that polynomial
continuous valuations are dense in the space of all continuous
valuations. However during the preparation of this paper we found
a gap in our original argument. So we do not know if this fact is
true.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- theorem-1: body_md -->
There exists a unique filtration $W_i$ on $PVal^{sm}(V)$ such that

(1) $\{W_i\}$ is compatible with the multiplicative structure,
i.e. $W_i \cdot W_j \subset W_{i+j}$;

(2) $\gamma_{i+1}\subset W_i\subset \gamma_i \mbox{ for all } i;$

(3) $W_0=\gamma_0,\,W_1 =\gamma_1$;

(4) $W_i$ is a closed subspace of $PVal^{sm}(V)$;

(5) $W_i$ is $Aff (V)$-invariant.
<!-- end theorem-1 -->
<!-- theorem-2: body_md -->
There exists a canonical isomorphism of graded algebras
$$gr_W (PVal^{sm}(V))\simeq Val^{sm}(V) \otimes \mathbb{C}[V]$$
where the $i$th graded term in the right hand side is equal to
$Val_i^{sm}(V)\otimes \mathbb{C}[V]$ where $\mathbb{C}[V]$ denotes the algebra
of polynomial functions on $V$.
<!-- end theorem-2 -->
<!-- theorem-3: body_md -->
The natural representations of the group $GL(V)$ in $Val_i^0(V)$
and $Val_i^1(V)$ are irreducible.
<!-- end theorem-3 -->
<!-- theorem-4: body_md -->
The maps $$(Val_i^0(V))^{sm}\to ((Val_{n-i}^{0}(V))^*)^{sm}\otimes
Val_n(V), \, \mbox{ and }$$ $$ (Val_i^1(V))^{sm}\to
((Val_{n-i}^{1}(V))^*)^{sm}\otimes Val_n(V)$$ induced by the
multiplication $(Val_i^0(V))^{sm}\otimes (Val_{n-i}^0(V))^{sm}\to
Val_n(V)$ and  $(Val_i^1(V))^{sm}\otimes (Val_{n-i}^1(V))^{sm}\to
Val_n(V)$, are isomorphisms.
<!-- end theorem-4 -->
<!-- theorem-5: body_md -->
Assume that $G$ is a compact subgroup of $GL(V)$ acting
transitively on the projective space $\mathbb{P}(V)$.

(i)Then $Val^G(V)$ is finite dimensional.

(ii) $Val^G(V)\subset Val^{sm}(V).$

(iii) $Val^G(V)$ is a finite dimensional graded subalgebra of
$Val^{sm}(V)$ satisfying Poincar\'e duality:
$$Val^G_i(V)\otimes Val_{n-i}^G(V)\longrightarrow Val_n^G(V)=\mathbb{C}\cdot vol$$
is a perfect pairing. In particular $h_i=h_{n-i}$.

(iv) $Val_1^G(V)$ is spanned by the intrinsic volume $V_1$, and
$Val^G_{n-1}(V)$ is spanned by the intrinsic volume $V_{n-1}$
where the intrinsic volumes are taken with respect to a
$G$-invariant Euclidean metric. Thus $h_1=h_{n-1}=1$.

(v) Assume in addition that $-Id\in G$. Then the numbers $h_i$
satisfy the Lefschetz inequalities:
$$h_i\leq h_{i+1} \mbox{ for } i<n/2.$$
<!-- end theorem-5 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
${\cal G}(V)\cap PVal^{sm}(V)$ is dense in $PVal^{sm}(V)$.
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
Let $\phi_1,\dots, \phi_s \in {\cal G}(V)$. Then there exists a linear
space $V'$, a linear imbedding $f:V\hookrightarrow V'$, smooth
measures $\mu_i$ on $V'$, and $A_1,\dots, A_s \in {\cal K}(V')$ such
that $\phi_i(K)=\mu_i(f(K)+A_i),\, i=1,\dots ,s$.
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
(i) For $\phi \in{\cal G}(V), \, \psi\in {\cal G}(W)$ their
exterior product $\phi\boxtimes  \psi \in {\cal G}(V\times W)$ is
well defined.

(ii) The exterior product is bilinear   with respect to each
argument.

(iii) Fix $\phi \in {\cal G} (V)$. Then the map ${\cal G} (W)\longrightarrow {\cal G}
(V\times W)$ given by $\psi\mapsto \phi \boxtimes \psi$ extends
(uniquely) by continuity to a map $CVal(V)\longrightarrow CVal(V\times W)$.

(iv)
$$(\phi \boxtimes \psi)\boxtimes \eta= \phi \boxtimes (\psi\boxtimes
\eta).$$

(v) Let $f:V\hookrightarrow V_1,\, g:W\hookrightarrow W_1$ be two
imbeddings. Let $\phi \in {\cal G}(V_1),\, \psi\in {\cal G}(W_1)$. Then
$$(f\times g)^*(\phi\boxtimes \psi)=f^*\phi \boxtimes g^*\psi.$$
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
Equipped with the above defined multiplication, ${\cal G}(V)$ becomes
an associative commutative unital algebra where the unit is the
Euler characteristic $\chi$.
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
Let ${\cal F}$ be a Fr\'echet $G$-module. Let $S$ be a finite
dimensional $G$-module. Then $({\cal F}\otimes S)^{sm}={\cal
F}^{sm}\otimes S$.
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- theorem-6: body_md -->
\label{casselman-wallach}
 Let $G$ be a real
reductive Lie group. Let $(\rho,G,{\cal F})$ and $(\pi,G,{\cal G})$ be
continuous representations of $G$ of moderate growth in Fr\'echet spaces ${\cal F}$ and
${\cal G}$. Assume in addition that ${\cal G}$ is an admissible $G$-module
of finite length, and
$${\cal F}^{sm}={\cal F},\, {\cal G}^{sm}={\cal G}.$$
Then any continuous morphism of $G$-modules $f:{\cal F}\to {\cal G}$ has
closed image.
<!-- end theorem-6 -->
<!-- theorem-7: body_md -->
\label{schwartz}
 Let $X_1$and $X_2$ be compact smooth
manifolds. Let ${\cal E}_1$ and ${\cal E}_2$ be smooth finite dimensional
vector bundles over $X_1$ and $X_2$ respectively. Let ${\cal G}$ be a
Fr\'echet space. Let
$$B:C^\infty(X_1,{\cal E}_1)\times C^\infty(X_2,{\cal E}_2)\to {\cal G}$$
be a continuous bilinear map. Then there exists unique continuous
linear operator
$$b:C^\infty(X_1\times X_2,{\cal E}_1\boxtimes {\cal E}_2)\to {\cal G}$$
such that $b(f_1\otimes f_2)=B(f_1,f_2)$ for any $f_i\in
C^\infty(X_i,{\cal E}_i),\, i=1,2$.
<!-- end theorem-7 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
The map $\Theta_d$  has a dense image.
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
The map $\Theta_d$ is an epimorphism.
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
The multiplication $$(PVal_i(V))^{sm}\otimes (PVal_j(V))^{sm}\longrightarrow
(PVal_{i+j}(V))^{sm}$$ is continuous.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- theorem-8: body_md -->
(i) The map $(Val_i^{0}(V))^{sm}\otimes
(Val_{n-i}^{0}(V))^{sm}\longrightarrow Val_n(V)$ is a perfect pairing. More
precisely the induced map
$$(Val_i^{0}(V))^{sm}\longrightarrow (Val_{n-i}^{0}(V)^*)^{sm}\otimes
Val_n(V)$$ is an isomorphism.

(ii) For $1\leq i\leq n-1$, the map $(Val_i^{1}(V))^{sm}\otimes
(Val_{n-i}^{1}(V))^{sm}\longrightarrow Val_n(V)$ is a perfect pairing in the
above sense.
<!-- end theorem-8 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
Let $V$ be an $n$-dimensional Euclidean space. Let
$$\phi(K)=V(K[i],A_1,\dots, A_{n-i}),\,
\psi(K)=V(K[n-i],B_1,\dots,B_i)$$ where $A_p,\, B_q \in {\cal K} (V)$
are fixed. Then
$$(\phi \cdot \psi)(K)={n\choose i}^{-1}V(A_1,\dots,
A_{n-i},-B_1,\dots, -B_{i}) vol(K).$$
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- claim-1: body_md -->
$$V(K[i],A_1,\dots, A_{n-i})=(n(n-1)\dots
(i+1))^{-1}\frac{\partial^{n-i}}{\partial \lambda_1 \dots \partial \lambda_{n-i}}\bigg
|_{0} vol (K+\sum _{j=1}^{n-i} \lambda_j A_j).$$
<!-- end claim-1 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
Let $X=Y\oplus Z$ be an orthogonal decomposition of a Euclidean
space $X$. Let $\dim X=N,\, \dim Y=n$. Let $M\in {\cal K}(Y),\,
A_1,\dots A_{N-n}\in {\cal K}(X).$ Then
$$V_N(M[n]; A_1,\dots A_{N-n})={N\choose n}^{-1}
vol_n(M)V_{N-n}(Pr_ZA_1,\dots ,Pr_ZA_{N-n})$$ where $Pr_Z$ denotes
the orthogonal projection onto $Z$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
The multiplication $$(Val^{\varepsilon}_1(V))^{sm}\otimes
(Val^{\varepsilon}_1(V))^{sm}\longrightarrow (Val^{0}_{2}(V))^{sm}$$ is non-zero for
$\varepsilon\in \mathbb{Z}/2\mathbb{Z}$ and hence has a dense image.
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- theorem-9: body_md -->
There exists an isomorphism of graded algebras $\mathbb{C}[x]/(x^{n+1})
\simeq Val^{O(n)}(V)$ given by $x\mapsto V_1$.
<!-- end theorem-9 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
For any $d$
$$W_i(PVal_d^{sm})\cap Val^{sm}(V)=Val_i^{sm}(V)\oplus Val_{i+1}^{sm}(V)\oplus \dots
\oplus Val_n^{sm}(V).$$
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- claim-2: body_md -->
$$\psi \cdot W_i(PVal_d^{sm}) =0.$$
<!-- end claim-2 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
$W_i(PVal_d^{sm})$ is  a closed subspace of $PVal_d^{sm}$.
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
Let $\phi \in PVal_d^{sm}$. If $\phi \in W_i( PVal_{d'}^{sm})$ for
some $d'\geq d$ then
$$\lim_{r\longrightarrow +0} \frac{1}{r^{i-1}}\phi(rK+x)=0 \, \forall x\in
X,\, \forall K\in {\cal K} (V).\eqno{(\star)}$$ Conversely if the
condition $(\star)$ holds then $\phi \in W_i(PVal_d^{sm})$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
(i) For $d'>d$ $W_i(PVal_{d'}^{sm})\cap
PVal_d^{sm}=W_i(PVal_d^{sm}).$

(ii) Let $f:U\longrightarrow V$ be an injective imbedding of linear spaces.
Then $f^*(W_i(PVal_d^{sm}(V)))\subset W_i(PVal_d^{sm}(U))$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- theorem-10: body_md -->
$$W_{i_1}(PVal_{d_1}^{sm})\otimes
W_{i_2}(PVal_{d_2}^{sm})\subset W_{i_1+i_2}(PVal_{d_1
+d_2}^{sm}).$$
<!-- end theorem-10 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
(i) For any $i$
$$\gamma_{i+1}\subset W_i\subset \gamma_i.$$

(ii) $W_1=\gamma_1.$
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- theorem-11: body_md -->
Assume that we have another filtration $\{\tilde W_i\}$ on $PVal^{sm}$
such that

(1) $\{\tilde W_i\}$ is compatible with the multiplicative structure,
i.e. $\tilde W_i \cdot \tilde W_j \subset \tilde W_{i+j}$;

(2) $\gamma_{i+1}\subset \tilde W_i\subset \gamma_i \mbox{ for all }
i.$

(3) $\tilde W_0=\gamma_0,\,\tilde W_1 =\gamma_1$;

(4) $\tilde W_i\cap PVal_d^{sm}$ is a closed subspace of $PVal_d^{sm}$
for all $i,\, d$.

(5) $\tilde W_i$ is $Aff (V)$-invariant.

Then $\tilde W_i=W_i$.
<!-- end theorem-11 -->
<!-- theorem-12: body_md -->
There exists a canonical isomorphism of graded algebras
$$gr_W (PVal^{sm}(V))\simeq Val^{sm}(V) \otimes \mathbb{C}[V]$$
where the $i$th graded term in the right side is equal to
$Val_i^{sm}(V)\otimes \mathbb{C}[V]$ where $\mathbb{C}[V]$ denote the algebra of
polynomial functions on $V$.
<!-- end theorem-12 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
The graded algebra $Val^{O(\infty)}= Val^{SO(\infty)}$ is
isomorphic to the graded algebra of polynomials in one variable
$\mathbb{C}[x]$ with the grading given by the degree of a polynomial.
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
Let $i_n:\mathbb{C}^n\hookrightarrow \mathbb{C}^{n+1}$ be the standard Hermitian
imbedding such that the last coordinate vanishes. For any $k$ the
restriction map $i_n^*: Val_k^{U(n+1)}(\mathbb{C}^{n+1})\longrightarrow
Val_k^{U(n)}(\mathbb{C}^n)$ is an isomorphism provided $n\geq k$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- definition-3: body_md -->
Let $(\pi,G,V)$ be a smooth representation of $G$ in a Fr\'echet
space $V$ (namely $V^{sm}=V$). One says that this representation
has {\itshape moderate growth} if for each continuous semi-norm
$\lambda$ on $V$ there exists a continuous semi-norm $\nu_\lambda$
on $V$ and $d_{\lambda}\in \mathbb{R}$ such that
$$\lambda(\pi(g)v)\leq ||g||^{d_\lambda}\nu_{\lambda}(v)$$
for $g\in G,\, v\in V$.
<!-- end definition-3 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{wall}
(i) If $(\pi,G,H)$ is a continuous representation of $G$ in a
Banach space $H$ then $(\pi,G,H^{sm})$ has moderate growth.

(ii) If $(\pi, G,V)$ is a representation of moderate growth. Let
$W$ be a closed $G$-invariant subspace of $V$. Then $W$ and $V/W$
have moderate growth.
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{obvious}
Let $G_1$ be a closed reductive subgroup of a reductive group $G$.
Assume that the image of $G_1$ in $GL(N,\mathbb{R})$ under the map
$p:G\hookrightarrow GL(N,\mathbb{R})$ is closed under the transposition.
Let $(\pi,G,H)$ has moderate growth. Then the restriction of this
representation to $G_1$ also has moderate growth.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{pval-banach}
The space $PVal_d(V)$ is a Banach space.
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{pval-mod}
$PVal_d^{sm}(V)$ has moderate growth as $GL(V)$-module.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- proposition-10: body_md -->
\label{prop}
In the notation of Section 1, the space $\Omega_d^n\otimes
C^\infty((\mathbb{P}_+(V^*))^k,L^{\boxtimes k})$ has moderate growth as
$GL(V)$-module.
<!-- end proposition-10 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop-gen}
Let the group $GL(V)$ act transitively on compact smooth manifolds
$X_1,\dots,X_k$. Let ${\cal E}_i$ be a finite dimensional
$GL(V)$-equivariant vector bundle over $X_i$, $i=1,\dots,k$. Then
the space $C^\infty(X_1\times \dots \times X_k, {\cal E}_1\times
\dots\times {\cal E}_k)$ has moderate growth as $GL(V)$-module.
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
